assessment: This fundamental study demonstrates that a point mutation resulting in dilated cardiomyopathy in human cardiac myosin increases the fraction of molecules that adopt the auto-inhibited super-relaxed conformation. This provides a mechanism for the lower force output observed in the hearts of affected individuals. The data supporting this, utilizing kinetic methods, a FRET-biosensor to detect conformational changes, and electron microscopy are convincing.
